locator.text: Equation (C.6), p. 159, in the proof of Lemma C.1

evidence: paper: \partial_\mu \{ g(2 \mu p) - 2 g(\mu p) \} \;=\; 2 p \{ g'(2 \mu p) - g'(\mu p) \} \;>\; 0.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The symbol g = log M_e never appears in the Lean, and no declaration states (C.6) in the variable μ with the factor 2p. What is stated is the same chain rule after two changes of packaging. (i) Variable: Lean differentiates in s = μp, so the factor 2p of the paper is a factor 2; the paper's derivative is p times the Lean's. (ii) Exponentiation: Lean differentiates V itself, baseVariance s = e^{g(2s) - 2g(s)} - 1, rather than the exponent. `baseVariance_hasDerivAt` gives deriv = 2 (baseVariance s + 1)(logSlope 2s - logSlope s); since logSlope = M_e'/M_e = g' by `normalizer_hasDerivAt` and `expNormalizer_pos`, and baseVariance s + 1 = e^{g(2s)-2g(s)} > 0, dividing by that positive factor and multiplying by p returns the paper's identity exactly. The positivity is likewise present and covers both signs the paper claims: for p > 0, μ > 0 the inequality is `logSlope_strictMono` (which rests on `moment_determinant_pos`, the paper's g'' > 0 as a tilted variance) via `baseVariance_deriv_pos`; for p < 0, μp < 0 and `baseVariance_deriv_neg` supplies deriv < 0, so p · deriv > 0 again. The conclusion the paper draws from (C.6), "V increases strictly with μ > 0, also when p = 0", is stated in full generality as `tiltVariance_strictMonoOn`, which is proved through `scaledRoot`/`signedRoot_deriv_pos` and so does not need the p ≠ 0 split at all.
